tools.name: fetch_url
tools.description: Send a request through the corsproxy.dev proxy with your API key and return the status, CORS and rate-limit headers, and body. Use it to test an integration or debug a CORS/proxy error. Counts against the daily quota.

tools.name: check_quota
tools.description: Today's request limit, used, and remaining for this key's account, and when the counter resets.

tools.name: explain_error
tools.description: Explain a corsproxy.dev reason key (the `code` in a rejected response, e.g. API_KEY_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED): status, meaning, and fix.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "explain_error" references sensitive artifacts (api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Explain a corsproxy.dev reason key (the `code` in a rejected response, e.g. API_KEY_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED): status, meaning, and fix.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "explain_error" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch_url · Private data: fetch_url · Public sink: fetch_url.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch_url · Private data: fetch_url · Public sink: fetch_url

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
